cve_summary: coders/jpeg.c in ImageMagick before 7.0.6-1 allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (application crash) or possibly have unspecified other impact via JPEG data that is too short.
docstring:
Summary: RegisterJPEGImage() adds JPEG image format properties to the supported formats list in the image processing library.

Parameters: N/A

Returns: size_t: the size of the registered JPEG image format entry.

Logic: The function initializes a version string and a description for the JPEG format. It creates multiple entries for different JPEG-related format identifiers (e.g., "JPE", "JPEG", "JPG", "JPS", "PJPEG") using the SetMagickInfo function. For each entry, it sets properties such as the decoder and encoder functions, thread support, and MIME type. The function checks the JPEG library version to determine thread support and assigns the appropriate handlers for reading and writing JPEG images. Each entry is registered using RegisterMagickInfo, ensuring that the library recognizes these formats for image processing tasks. The function handles the versioning and format specifics to maintain compatibility with different JPEG library versions.

judge_vs_vulnerable.rationale: The two implementations are identical in their logic and behavior. Both register the same set of JPEG-related format identifiers with the same properties, including thread support, decoder/encoder handlers, MIME type, and version information. There are no observable differences in the output or behavior for any input.

judge_vs_fixed.rationale: The two implementations are identical in code and logic. They both register JPEG image format entries with the same properties, including versioning, thread support, decoder/encoder handlers, and MIME type. There is no observable behavioral difference between the two.
